discovery: Spectroscopic detection and characterization of exoplanet atmospheres through transmission and emission spectroscopy

nominees.name: David Charbonneau
nominees.affiliation: Harvard University, Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian, USA

nominees.name: Drake Deming
nominees.affiliation: University of Maryland, College Park, USA

subfield: Astrophysics (exoplanets, molecular spectroscopy of planetary atmospheres)
motivation: Charbonneau's 2002 detection of sodium in the atmosphere of HD 209458b opened a new observational window: the physical and chemical composition of planets around other stars. Seager's theoretical framework for transmission spectra predicted which atomic and molecular signatures would be observable and how to interpret them through radiative transfer and atmospheric physics. In 2005 Deming and Charbonneau independently made the first detections of thermal emission from exoplanets using Spitzer secondary eclipses, which made it possible to measure planetary temperatures and energy budgets directly. These techniques now underpin JWST's detections of water, CO2, CO, SO2 and photochemistry in exoplanet atmospheres. Together they link fundamental molecular physics to the question of how planets form and what they are made of, including the delivery of water and volatiles, and they set the path towards searching for habitable worlds.
